example_sentence: He emigrated to Belgium.

definition_zh: n. 爆炸；爆发；激增

definition_zh: adj. 恶毒的；恶意的；堕落的；有错误的；品性不端的；剧烈的；n. (Vicious)人名；(英)维舍斯

example_sentence: Sarah can be quite vicious at times.

definition_zh: adj. 被动的，消极的；被动语态的；n. 被动语态

example_sentence: Kathy seems to take a very passive role in the relationship.

definition_zh: adj. 吵闹的，喧嚣的；难驾驭的

definition_zh: n. 罚金；没收物；丧失的东西；adj. 因受罚而丧失的；被没收的；v. （因犯罪、失职、违约等）丧失（权利、名誉、生命等）

example_sentence: The company’s property may even be forfeit.

definition_zh: v. 修饰；装饰；润色
etymology: em + bell (美) + ish → 使…美 → 装饰
example_sentence: The boat was embellished with carvings in red and blue.

definition_zh: n. 深仇；怨恨；敌意

definition_zh: v. 封锁；n. 阻塞

definition_zh: n. 笨拙；无礼

definition_zh: n. 法定人数

example_sentence: We need a quorum of seven.

definition_zh: adj. 繁重的；麻烦的；负有义务的；负有法律责任的
etymology: oner (劳动) + ous → 繁重的
example_sentence: an onerous task

definition_zh: adj. 外来的；没有关联的；来自体外的

example_sentence: extraneous noises

definition_zh: n. 管；电子管；隧道；电视机；v. 使成管状；把…装管；用管输送

definition_zh: n. 强制；强迫；强制力
etymology: com + puls (推) + ion → 一起推 → 强迫
example_sentence: The use of compulsion in psychiatric care cannot be justified.

definition_zh: n. 倾向，爱好；斜坡
etymology: in (在…中) + clin (倾斜) + ation → 倾斜到…中 → 有倾向 → 倾向
example_sentence: My natural inclination was to say no.

definition_zh: adj. 异国的；外来的；异国情调的
etymology: ex (出) + ot + ic (…的) → 外面的 → 外来的
example_sentence: exotic birds

definition_zh: adj. 可感知的；可评估的；相当可观的

example_sentence: There’s no appreciable change in the patient’s condition.

definition_zh: n. 设施；设备；容易；灵巧

example_sentence: What recreational facilities are now available?

definition_zh: adj. 等距的；距离相等的
example_sentence: Altus is equidistant from Ozark and Cotton Town.

example_sentence: Several passengers were leaning against the ship’s rail.

example_sentence: It’s impossible for me to give you a definite answer.

definition_zh: v. 剥夺；使裸露

definition_zh: adj. 粗野的；粗鲁的；粗鄙的；笨拙的；乡土气的

definition_zh: adj. 唐吉诃德式的；狂想家的；愚侠的
etymology: qui + xotic (看作exotic， 奇异的) → 奇异的事物有很多都是不切实际的， 比如唐吉诃德式的人物 → 唐吉诃德式的

example_sentence: a hideous dress

example_sentence: But presently we have no concrete prescript in the field. This thesis is trying to solve this problem.

example_sentence: John was as bouncy and ebullient as Helen was diffident and reserved.

example_sentence: ‘Be prepared’ is the motto of the Boy Scouts.

example_sentence: She rushes from job to job at a frenetic pace.

example_sentence: An anonymous benefactor donated $2 million.

definition_zh: adj. 占优势的；突出的；压倒性的
etymology: 来自preponder (ate) (压倒) + ant → 压倒性的 → 占有优势的

definition_zh: n. 软骨
etymology: “咔踢得折” → 软骨咔一踢就折了 → 软骨
example_sentence: Andre Agassi has pulled out of next week's Grand Slam Cup after tearing a cartilage in his chest.

definition_zh: adj. 假的；伪造的；欺骗的
etymology: 来自spuri (a) (伪造的作品) + ous → 伪造的
example_sentence: spurious sympathy

definition_zh: n. 用词不当；误称；写错姓名
etymology: mis (错误) + nom (名字) + er → 名字用错了 → 误称
example_sentence: ‘Silent movie’ is a misnomer since the movies usually had a musical accompaniment.

definition_zh: adj. 防腐的，抗菌的；非常整洁的；n. 防腐剂，抗菌剂
etymology: anti (反) + sept (菌) + ic → 杀菌剂
example_sentence: Because of its irritating effect on humans, the use ofphenol as a general antiseptic has been largely discontinued.

definition_zh: adj. 集体的；共同的；集合的；集体主义的；n. 集团；集合体；集合名词
etymology: 和collect (v. 收集)一起记
example_sentence: a collective decision made by all board members

definition_zh: adj. 流行的；普遍的，广传的
etymology: pre (前) + val (强壮的) + ent → 走在时尚的前沿 → 流行的
example_sentence: the prevalent belief in astrology

definition_zh: adj. 呕吐的；不稳定的；催吐的
etymology: qu (看作quite, 很) + easy (轻松) → 笑一笑， 十年少， 不必忧虑 → 忧虑的
example_sentence: The sea got rougher, and I began to feel queasy.

definition_zh: n. 迷惑，欺骗；错觉；幻想
etymology: de + lus (扮演) + ion (表示名词) → 扮演出假象， 使产生错觉 → 错觉
example_sentence: I was under the delusion that he intended to marry me.

definition_zh: n. [生化] 分解代谢
example_sentence: These processes are called anabolism and catabolism.

definition_zh: vt. 烧窑；在干燥炉干燥；n. （砖，石灰等的）窑；炉；干燥炉
etymology: 煤窑 (kiln) 倒塌杀死 (kill) 了许多人

definition_zh: v. 等待；面临；禁得起
example_sentence: They are stronger than us and can afford to bide their time.

definition_zh: adj. 主观的；个人的；自觉的
etymology: subject (主题) + ive → 主观的
example_sentence: As a critic, he is far too subjective.

definition_zh: adj. 货币的；财政的
etymology: monet (看作money， 货币) + ary (…的) → 货币的
example_sentence: the government’s tight monetary policy

definition_zh: v. 滤过；渗入；慢慢传开；n. 滤波器；[化工] 过滤器；筛选；滤光器
example_sentence: The water in the tank is constantly filtered.

definition_zh: adj. 不可救药的；积习难改的；n. 不可救药的人
etymology: in (不) + corrig (看作correct ， 正确的) + ible (可以…的) → 不可以改正的
example_sentence: "Sunita, you are incorrigible!" he said.

definition_zh: n. 骑士精神（复数chivalries）；骑士制度
etymology: chiv (刀) + alry → 立马横刀 → 骑士精神； 骑士制度
example_sentence: ...the age of chivalry.

definition_zh: n. 成分；选民；委托人；adj. 构成的；选举的
etymology: con + stit ( = stat， 站) + uent → 站在一起 → 成分
example_sentence: He told his constituents that he would continue to represent them to the best of his ability.

definition_zh: adj. 可怕的；令人敬畏的
etymology: re (反复) + doubt (疑虑) + able → 千古奇案， 疑云迭起 → 可怕的
example_sentence: He had never met a more redoubtable fighter.

definition_zh: adj. 无价的；非常贵重的
etymology: in (无) + valuable (有价值的) → 无价的
example_sentence: I was able to gain invaluable experience over that year.

definition_zh: n. 代理；代用品；遗嘱检验法官；vt. 代理；指定某人为自己的代理人；adj. 代理的；替代的
etymology: sur (外) + rog (要求) + ate (使) → 要求将代理者排除在外 → 代理者
example_sentence: Arms control should not be made into a surrogate for peace.

definition_zh: n. [解剖] 食管；[解剖] 食道
example_sentence: Do not attempt to force the dog to vomit as this can burn the esophagus and stomach and cause further complications.

definition_zh: n. 参数；系数；参量
example_sentence: ...some of the parameters that determine the taste of a wine.

definition_zh: v. 掩饰，掩盖；假装
etymology: dis (否定) + semble (相同) → 不和 (本来面目) 相同 → 掩饰
example_sentence: Henry was not slow to dissemble when it served his purposes.

definition_zh: n. 命令；顺序；规则；[贸易] 定单；v. 命令；整理；定购
example_sentence: There seemed to be no logical order to the sections.

definition_zh: adj. 上诉的；受理上诉的
etymology: 和appeal (v. 上诉； 呼吁) 一起记
example_sentence: In some recent years, law students who apply to clerk for federal appellate judges were hired almost two years before they would graduate and begin work.

definition_zh: adj. 精神的；心灵的；灵魂的；超自然的；n. 灵媒；巫师
etymology: psych (精神) + ic → 精神的
example_sentence: a spiritual healer with psychic powers

definition_zh: n. 替罪羊，替人顶罪者；替身；vt. 使成为…的替罪羊
etymology: scape (看作escape， 逃跑) + goat (羊) → 狼逃跑了找羊替罪 → 替罪羊
example_sentence: I don't think I deserve to be made the scapegoat for a couple of bad results.

definition_zh: n. 推测；猜想；v. 推测；揣摩
etymology: con + ject (推， 扔) + ure → 全部是推出来的 → 推测
example_sentence: What she said was pure conjecture .

definition_zh: adj. 习惯的；惯常的；习以为常的
etymology: 来自habit (n. 习惯)
example_sentence: James took his habitual morning walk around the garden.

definition_zh: adj. 必备的，必不可少的；需要的；n. 必需品
etymology: re + quisite (寻求) → 反复寻求是必要的 → 必要的
example_sentence: He lacks the requisite qualifications.

definition_zh: adj. 坚定的；不变的
etymology: stead (看作stand站， 保持) + fast (牢固的) → 保持稳固 → 坚定的， 忠实的
example_sentence: her father’s steadfast love for her

definition_zh: v. 免除；豁免；adj. 被免除的；被豁免的；n. 免税者；被免除义务者
etymology: ex + empt (拿) → 拿走 → 被免除的
example_sentence: So we have the current argument over how much of the derivative market will be exempt from regulation.

definition_zh: v. 使贬值；贬低；轻视
etymology: de (否定) + preciate (看作appreciate， 欣赏) → 不欣赏 → 反对
example_sentence: New cars depreciate in value quickly.

definition_zh: n. [地物] 极光；曙光
etymology: 奥罗拉， 古希腊传说中的曙光女神
example_sentence: The light creates the aurora that we see.

definition_zh: n. 起源；原点；出身；开端
etymology: ori (开始) + gin → 开始 → 来源， 起点
example_sentence: The tradition has its origins in the Middle Ages.

definition_zh: adj. 同音的；和谐的
example_sentence: A harmonious campus pays more attention to an all-round, humane, unisonous , sustainable and diverse education;

definition_zh: n. 超载；额外费；v. 追加罚款；使…装载过多；使…负担过重
etymology: sur (超过) + charge (收费) → 额外收费

definition_zh: adj. 艳丽的；火焰似的；炫耀的；n. 凤凰木
etymology: flam (火焰) + boyant → 火焰似的
example_sentence: He lifted his arms in a flamboyant gesture .

definition_zh: n. 勤勉；刻苦；殷勤
etymology: as + sid (坐) + uity → 坐着一动不动地学习 → 刻苦

definition_zh: v. 分层；成层；使形成阶层
etymology: strat (层次) + ify (使) → 使分层

definition_zh: n. 镇静；沉着
etymology: com + pos (放) + ure (状态) → 放着不动 → 沉着
example_sentence: He has lost his composure under the pressure of the situation.

definition_zh: adj. 决定性的；果断的，坚定的
etymology: 来自decision (n. 决定)
example_sentence: a decisive leader

definition_zh: n. 管理人；行政官
etymology: 来自administrate (v. 管理； 支配)
example_sentence: On Friday the company's administrators sought permission from a Melbourne court to keep operating.

definition_zh: n. 环境；上下文；来龙去脉
etymology: con (共同) + text (编织) → 共同编织在一起 → 上下文
example_sentence: The meaning of ‘mad’ depends on its context. mad

definition_zh: n. 伪造；伪造罪；伪造物
etymology: 来自forge (v. 伪造)
example_sentence: The painting was a very clever forgery.

definition_zh: v. 暗示；使逐渐而巧妙地取得；使迂回地潜入
etymology: in (进入) + sinu (弯曲) + ate → 曲折地进入主题 → 含沙射影地说
example_sentence: What are you trying to insinuate?

definition_zh: n. 客户；诉讼委托人
etymology: 来自client (n. 当事人， 顾客)； clientele是集合名词
example_sentence: This pub had a mixed clientele.
